description:
src/backend.rs:135-140 — the rustdoc on CalendarsBackend::supports_type is five lines:

    /// Returns `true` if this account supports the given JMAP object type.
    ///
    /// Called by the server consumer (e.g. session capability builder) — NOT
    /// called internally by the handler library. Backends that support all
    /// types unconditionally can return `true` always.

The canonical mail-server's MailBackend::supports_type doc at
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:254-295 carries four explicit sections:

  # Contract: "global, stateless backend-capability check ... not 'does this
              user's account have this type enabled?'. That is why the
              method is synchronous and takes no caller or account_id
              arguments."
  # Types in scope: list of JMAP object types this trait covers
  # Callers: "The handler library calls this method when handling optional
            methods. For example, handle_search_snippet_get returns
            accountNotSupportedByMethod when supports_type::<SearchSnippet>()
            is false ..."
  # Default: guidance for backends that support every type unconditionally

The calendars doc disagrees with mail's doc on a substantive point: calendars
says "NOT called internally by the handler library" but mail explicitly says
the handler library DOES call it (snippet fast-path). Both are accurate per
crate, but neither doc says "scope of this contract is only my crate's
handlers" — so a backend author cookie-cutting a single supports_type impl
that's intended to work across both extensions reads two contradictory
contracts.

What goes wrong for the caller: a backend author writes a calendars+mail
shared backend, returns `false` for unsupported types per calendars' doc, and
inadvertently disables mail-server's snippet short-circuit. Or a calendars
backend author copies the mail-server pattern of "always return true" and
wires no per-type gating, breaking session-capability building when calendars
is enabled per-account.

Fix: mirror the canonical four-section structure. Specifically state that
the doc-contract is workspace-wide and reference the canonical sibling for
the cross-extension semantics. Or, if "handler library never calls it on
calendars" is intentional and provable from src/, document explicitly that
this is calendars-handler-library policy, not a property of supports_type
itself.
title: supports_type rustdoc lacks Contract/Types/Callers sections that canonical mail-server documents
